paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this room: Jesus doesn't wait for His people to get brave before He shows up. The disciples had the doors locked, and Jesus came and stood among them anyway. He didn't scold them. He said, "Peace be with you!" and then showed them His hands and His side (John 20:19-20). Then He told them, "As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you," which means the locked room was never where they were meant to stay (John 20:21).

Now let's talk about Thomas, because I think a lot of us see ourselves in him. He said what he needed, out loud, and I think that took honesty. Jesus didn't turn away from him. He came back and offered Thomas the very thing he asked for, then said, "Stop doubting and believe" (John 20:27). Thomas answered, "My Lord and my God!" (John 20:28). So bring your questions to Jesus, friend, because He's not afraid of them.

And here's the part that's for YOU. Jesus said, "blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed" (John 20:29). The writer says there were many other signs that aren't written in this book, but these ones are written "so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name" (John 20:30-31). That's why this passage is here. Believe in Jesus, friend, and in His name you have life.
